title: The Pale Visitor
premise: Sable Nystrom, a meticulous property surveyor, is hired to appraise Hollowmere House, an estate whose founders vanished in 1911 mid-ritual. As he catalogs the rooms, the mirrors begin lagging one second behind reality — and the reflection starts moving independently, showing him the house as it was when the ritual was interrupted. The house has been waiting for someone to finish what its founders started: binding the town's stolen dead into its walls. Sable must choose between completing the rite and becoming its final component, and he ends it by turning the mirror's borrowed second against the house, releasing the dead and letting Hollowmere collapse into the ground that was taken for it.
about_author: Cyrus Halloran spent nine years as a land surveyor in rural New England before turning to horror fiction full-time. His work draws on old property records, abandoned estates, and his conviction that every deed hides a debt.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Arriving at Hollowmere House to appraise it for a bank sale, Sable finds the rooms numbered in chalk by hands long gone and a ledger counting doors that don't match the blueprints. He keeps professional distance, but the house feels attentive. Emotional beat: unease disguised as competence — he trusts his measurements more than his instincts, and the measurements are already wrong.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Every mirror begins reflecting the room a heartbeat late; then his reflection stops mimicking him entirely and gestures toward the cellar. There he finds the founders' half-finished ritual circle and names of townspeople erased from every record. The reflection shows him 1911: the founders fleeing before sealing the rite. Emotional beat: dread curdling into compulsion — the house needs a finisher, and it has chosen him.

chapters.title: The Founders' Debt
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Trapped inside as doors multiply and vanish, Sable pieces together the truth: the founders built their fortune on land seized from families they then bound into the walls, and the ritual sustains their heirs' prosperity still. The heirs arrive demanding he complete it or die with the house. Emotional beat: fury and clarity — this isn't haunting, it's accounting, and justice outside the law means settling it himself.

chapters.title: Closing the Circle
chapters.summary: POV Sable. At midnight Sable stands in the circle with the heirs watching, and instead of binding the dead, he speaks their names back into the world, feeding the ritual's own stolen second into the reversal. The mirrors sync, then shatter; the heirs age to dust as the house folds inward. Sable walks out at dawn with an appraisal of zero. Emotional beat: grim peace — belonging found not in the house, but in refusing it.
